assessment.nobel_worthiness: Designing zeolite and molecular-sieve frameworks with controlled pore size, topology and active-site placement underlies refining, emissions control and selective catalysis at industrial scale. It is a clear case of structure determining function, and the structural chemistry of these frameworks is where my own expertise sits, so I can judge the evidence directly.
assessment.attribution: Corma (tailored acid and bifunctional zeolite catalysts), Davis (structure-directing design, new frameworks and pore architectures) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents such as SSZ-13 for commercial catalysts) are the strongest trio from the list. Tsapatsis and Yu are real contributors, but a three-person limit leaves them out, and some zeolite-synthesis priority questions go back to earlier industrial work.
assessment.maturity: The field is decades old with extensive independent confirmation and long industrial deployment. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will see this as a diffuse field rather than one discovery.
Priority relative to early industrial zeolite work is only partly reflected in the credited names.
I have not independently verified individual priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent in roughly a decade. The effect has been large in materials chemistry and energy research, and the defect tolerance and compositional tunability are chemically interesting.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park the first solid-state high-efficiency device, and Snaith the meso-superstructured and planar architectures. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also made decisive contributions, so the allocation is contested and the three-person limit is tight.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies and architectures are reproduced widely. Long-term operational stability and lead toxicity are not resolved, so recognition could be early for some committee members.
uncertainties: Contested credit among at least six people.
Device stability and commercial viability remain unproven.
Whether the committee treats this as chemistry or physics and energy engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography turned XFEL pulses into a way to get room-temperature structures from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage, and to follow time-resolved structural changes. It enables structure determination from samples that conventional methods cannot handle, a priority I share, and it has produced structures of membrane proteins and reaction intermediates.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first demonstration and the methodology, Hajdu the diffraction-before-destruction concept, and Fromme the nanocrystal sample work. Schlichting and others also contributed substantially, and credit around the concept is shared with others not on this list.
assessment.maturity: The method is established across several facilities, with growing independent confirmation. Time-resolved chemistry results are still maturing, but the technique itself is stable.
uncertainties: Weak overlap with the 2017 cryo-EM and earlier crystallography prizes may cut either way.
Complicated attribution in a large facility-driven field.
Impact is concentrated in a small number of facilities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase converts N2 to ammonia under ambient conditions. The structures of the MoFe protein and the FeMo cofactor with its central carbide, together with mechanistic work, explain a central metalloenzyme of the nitrogen cycle. It is rigorous structural and bioinorganic chemistry with clear evidence for the structure.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first MoFe protein structure and cofactor work), Einsle (the carbide and high-resolution structures) and Seefeldt (mechanism and spectroscopy) are a reasonable trio. Dean and Ribbe also contributed to biosynthesis, so credit is spread widely.
assessment.maturity: The core structures are firmly confirmed by independent groups. The catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding site are still debated, which weighs against a mechanism-based citation.
uncertainties: Whether the structural result alone is enough without a settled mechanism.
Important contributors outside the list, such as spectroscopists, may be missing from the credit.
Dividing credit between the structure and the mechanism is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Template-directed ordered mesoporous silica created a new class of porous solids with uniform, tunable mesopores, made through surfactant liquid-crystal templating. It opened a general route to hierarchical and nanostructured materials and is closely tied to the electron-microscopy and diffraction characterization of ordered pores.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil, M41S) have clear priority, Stucky and Zhao extended the work to SBA-15 and large pores, and Ryoo to ordered carbons and zeolite nanosheets. The Mobil group and Japanese earlier work (FSM-16) complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature with broad independent confirmation, and applications in catalysis, sorption and delivery are demonstrated. Peak influence may have passed, which weighs against timeliness.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil and the Japanese FSM-16 work.
Whether commercial and application impact is large enough.
Allocation among Kresge, Beck, Zhao, Stucky and Ryoo.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large and rapidly growing family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable composition and surface terminations. They are a clear inorganic-materials result, with demonstrated use in energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum authored the 2011 discovery and the group is well defined, with a straightforward three-person configuration. Naguib is a junior author, so the committee may weigh this.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is very broad, but the field is only about 15 years old. Practical applications and structural control of surface terminations are still developing, so recognition could be early.
uncertainties: Premature recognition risk.
Surface-termination structure is hard to determine and often only averaged.
Role of Naguib relative to the senior authors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts push atom efficiency to its limit and offer a clear way to link structure and activity in heterogeneous catalysis. Characterization by aberration-corrected electron microscopy and X-ray absorption is central to the claims.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Nature Chemistry paper by Qiao, Wang, Liu, Zhang and coworkers named the concept, and Liu contributed the electron microscopy. Earlier supported-atom work and the contributions of Datye, Wang and Li make priority and allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and widely replicated, but the stability and uniformity of single-atom sites, and real catalytic performance under reaction conditions, are still contested. Some claims depend on averaged spectroscopy rather than direct structure proof.
uncertainties: Evidence that isolated atoms are the true active sites is not always conclusive.
Priority questions about the concept.
Possibly premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of carbon nanotubes by electron microscopy, with the discovery of single-wall tubes in 1993, opened a major nanocarbon field. The structural identification was done by electron diffraction and HRTEM, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Iijima's 1991 observation is widely seen as decisive, and single-wall tubes were reported by Iijima and Ichihashi and independently by Bethune. Endo's earlier synthesis of carbon fibres and the Soviet 1952 report make historical priority disputed.
assessment.maturity: The structure is confirmed beyond doubt, and the field is mature. The applications have been slower than expected, and the discovery is old enough that the case is long-standing.
uncertainties: Historical priority disputes.
Overlap with the 1996 fullerene prize.
Applied impact has lagged the early expectations.
